data.Title: PEPPER is now available for PHPs!
data.Subtitle: PEPPER is now available for Partial Hospitalization Programs
data.Summary: PEPPER is now available for Partial Hospitalization Programs
data.Content:
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is pleased to announce the release of the Program for Evaluating Payment Patterns Electronic Report (PEPPER) for Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHPs), along with the supporting User Guide.

PEPPER is a valuable resource designed to support providers in evaluating their billing practices. By analyzing PEPPER data, facilities can:

  • Identify where billing practices may need adjustment
  • Detect areas that require auditing or monitoring
  • Recognize Diagnosis-Related Groups (DRGs) that may be at risk for under-coding or over-coding
  • Monitor trends in length of stay across target areas

Accessing PEPPER

Authorized Officials (AOs), Access Managers (AMs), and Staff End Users (SEUs) can now download their organization’s PEPPER from the PEPPER Portal.

To become an SEU and access your organization’s PEPPER:

  • Sign in to the CMS I&A System using your existing National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES) or Provider Enrollment, Chain, and Ownership (PECOS) credentials.
  • Request the PEPPER business function for your organization. The Comparative Billing Report (CBR) business function is also available and can be requested at the same time.
  • Your AO or AM must approve your request.

AOs and AMs can find step-by-step instructions in the Identity & Access (I&A) Management System Quick Reference Guide and Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

User Guide

Visit the CBR/PEPPER website for more information about the release and the PHP PEPPER User Guide.

Webinar

CMS will host a webinar on Thursday, September 24, 2026, at 12:00 pm CT (1:00 pm ET) to provide an overview of the relaunched PHP PEPPER. Register for the webinar today.

data.Title: Claims Processing Instructions for the Gene Therapy Drug, Encelto ™, Used in Ambulatory Surgical Centers (ASCs) and the Hospital Outpatient Departments (HOPDs)
data.Subtitle: Reminder to Bill Encelto on Multiple Claim Lines When Necessary
data.Summary: Reminder to Bill Encelto on Multiple Claim Lines When Necessary
data.Content:
Encelto™ is billable and payable, when reasonable and necessary, by hospital outpatient departments under the Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and by Ambulatory Surgical Centers (ASCs) under normal billing rules.

Practitioners must split charges to multiple claims and append modifiers LU (fractionated payment) and 76 (repeat service or payment by the same physician or other qualified healthcare professional) to their claims to facilitate proper payment. For more information, refer to our Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-Cell Therapy Billing Instructions resource.

data.Title: CMS IRF Provider Education Webinar: FY 2027 IRF Final Rule Updates
data.Subtitle: CMS Invites Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility (IRF) Providers to Join this Educational Event
data.Summary: CMS Invites Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility (IRF) Providers to Join this Educational Event
data.Content:
CMS will host a national provider education webinar for inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) providers on Tuesday, September 29, 2026, from 1 – 2 pm ET.

The webinar will review FY 2027 IRF Prospective Payment System (PPS) final rule policies and related Medicare coverage requirements, including revisions related to:

  • The 36-hour requirement 
  • Initial interdisciplinary team meeting requirements 
  • Documentation expectations related to these requirements

This webinar is intended to help IRF providers understand finalized rule revisions, support consistent application of Medicare coverage requirements, and reduce the risk of documentation and billing errors.

Who should attend:
IRF administrators, rehabilitation physicians, therapy directors, clinicians, compliance staff, billing staff, and other staff involved in IRF coverage, documentation, or billing requirements.

Webinar details:
Date: Tuesday, September 29, 2026
Time: 1 – 2 pm ET
Registration link: https://cms.zoomgov.com/webinar/register/WN_fShdGivpTUW48qog-fFM0g 
Materials: Will be available prior to the event

Providers may submit questions about webinar logistics, webinar materials, or webinar content to IRFCoverage@cms.hhs.gov.

data.Title: MolDX: Biomarker Testing for Risk Stratification in DCIS: October 13, 2026
data.Subtitle: Join WPS and Other MACs for this Evidentiary CAC Meeting
data.Summary: Join WPS and other MACs for this Evidentiary CAC meeting.
data.Content:
Palmetto GBA, along with CGS Administrators, Noridian Healthcare Solutions, and WPS, will host a Multi-MAC Evidentiary Contractor Advisory Committee (CAC) Meeting via Microsoft Teams Webinar on October 13, 2026, from 1:00–3:00 pm CT (2:00–4:00 pm ET). Discussions will focus on Molecular Diagnostics (MolDX): Biomarker Testing for Risk Stratification in Ductal Carcinoma In Situ (DCIS).

Palmetto GBA previously held an Evidentiary CAC for this LCD on July 15, 2024. To ensure the most accurate information and balanced subject matter expert discussion, we are holding another Evidentiary CAC according to the following notice.

CMS assigned Medicare Administrative Contractors (MACs) the task of developing Local Coverage Determinations (LCDs). The purpose of the CAC meeting is to provide a formal mechanism for healthcare professionals to be informed of the evidence used in developing an LCD and promote communication between the MACs and the healthcare community. The CAC panel will discuss the clinical literature related to MolDX: Biomarker Testing for Risk Stratification in DCIS and rate their confidence in a series of key questions. Discussions will occur between Subject Matter Expert (SME) panelists and Contractor Medical Directors. The public may attend, but questions from the public will not be entertained. 

We invite interested stakeholders to listen via Microsoft Teams webinar, but advance registration is required. 

Register here: MoIDX CAC Meeting
You will receive your confirmation email once you complete registration.
Note: Registration deadline is October 12, 2026, 10:59 pm CT (11:59 pm ET).

Lines will remain muted throughout the conference except for the invited CAC panelists and the MAC hosts.

data.Title: New Medicare Enrollment Application - Clinics/Group Practices and Certain Other Suppliers (CMS-855B)
data.Subtitle: New CMS-855B
data.Summary: Updated Medicare Enrollment Application - Clinics/Group Practices and Certain Other Suppliers (CMS-855B)
data.Content:
CMS released the new Medicare Enrollment Application - Clinics/Group Practices and Certain Other Suppliers (CMS-855B). Updates were also made to the Provider Enrollment, Chain, and Ownership System (PECOS) to mirror the paper application.

MACs began accepting the new application on June 1, 2026, and stopped accepting the old version on August 3, 2026.

Updates to the application include:

  • Section verbiage and layout changes for improved clarity
  • New section 4H Reassignment of Benefit Information
  • Updated list of reportable adverse legal actions 
  • New submission reason of “You are solely enrolling in Medicare to participate in Medicaid or another health care program and will not bill Medicare”
